questions.chapter: Class as the Basis of Computation
questions.topic: Class Teacher: salary increment and income tax
concepts: class with data members and methods
questions.question:
Define a class Teacher described as below:
Data Members: Name, Address, Phone number, Highest Qualification, Subject Specialization, Monthly Salary, Income Tax.
Member Methods:
(i) To accept the details of a teacher.
(ii) To display the teacher's details.
(iii) To increment the monthly salary by 5000.
(iv) To compute the annual income tax as 5% of the annual salary above 150000.
Write a main method to create objects of the class and call the member methods.

marking_points.point: Class declaration with all seven data members of suitable types
accept() inputs all details using Scanner
increment() adds 5000 to monthly salary
computeTax(): annual = 12 x salary
Tax = 5% of (annual - 150000) only when annual > 150000, else 0
display() prints all details
main() creates object and calls methods in order
Variable description / comments

questions.question: Which of the following access control must be used for the main method to be invoked by the JVM?
questions.solution: (b) Public. The JVM calls main() from outside the class, so it must be public.

concepts: static members belong to the class
questions.question: Which of the following keywords helps access a class member without creating an object and without associating a variable with an object?
questions.solution: (c) Static. A static member belongs to the class and can be used through the class name without an object.

questions.question: The access modifier that gives least accessibility is:
questions.solution: (a) Private. Private members are visible only inside their own class.

questions.question: What is the scope of a private variable?

options.a: Within the class and its subclasses
options.b: Only within the class in which it is defined

questions.solution: (b) Only within the class in which it is defined. A private member cannot be used outside the class that declares it, not even by subclasses.

questions.question: Which access modifier allows variables to be accessible in all classes, including other packages?
questions.solution: (a) Public. Public members are visible to every class in every package.

questions.question: Which modifier restricts accessibility to the same class only?
questions.solution: (b) Private. Private limits access to the declaring class.

questions.question: What is encapsulation in object-oriented programming?

options.a: Binding methods and variables together in a class
options.c: Extending the functionality of a base class
options.d: Restricting variable access within a function

questions.solution: (a) Binding methods and variables together in a class. Encapsulation wraps data members and the methods that work on them into one unit, the class.

questions.question: What keyword is used to define class variables?
questions.solution: (c) Static. A variable declared static belongs to the class, so it is a class variable.

questions.question: Which type of variable is specific to each object of a class?
questions.solution: (b) Instance variable. Each object gets its own copy of every instance variable.

questions.question: Which of these is a non-access modifier in Java?
questions.solution: (c) Final. final changes a member's behaviour, not its visibility; the other three are access modifiers.

questions.question: Which access modifier allows variables to be accessible only in the same package?
questions.solution: (c) Default. With no modifier (default/friendly access) a member is visible only within its package.

questions.question: Which access modifier restricts variable inheritance to subclasses in the same or other packages?
questions.solution: (c) Protected. Protected members are visible in the same package and are inherited by subclasses in any package.

questions.topic: The four access levels in Java
questions.question: List the four access modifiers provided by Java.
questions.solution: public, protected, private and default (friendly / package access, when no modifier is written).

marking_points.point: Any two of public, protected, private, default
The other two

questions.question: What is the purpose of access modifiers?
questions.solution: Access modifiers control the visibility of a class's variables and methods, i.e. which classes and packages may use them. This protects data from unwanted access (data hiding) while letting the needed members be used from outside.

marking_points.point: They control visibility / accessibility of members
This protects data (data hiding / security)

marking_points.point: Scope limited to the method/block where declared
Correct example

questions.question: What are instance variables? Give an example.

marking_points.point: Definition: declared in class, outside methods, separate copy per object

questions.question: Differentiate between private and public access modifiers.
questions.solution:
private: the member can be used only inside the class in which it is declared.
public: the member can be used by every class, in the same package or in any other package.

marking_points.point: private: accessible only within its own class
public: accessible from all classes and packages

questions.question: What is a class variable? How is it declared?
questions.solution: A class variable belongs to the class, not to any object; only one copy exists and it is shared by all objects. It is declared with the keyword static, e.g. static int x;

marking_points.point: One copy shared by all objects / belongs to the class
Declared with static, with example

questions.question: Explain the scope of protected access modifiers.
questions.solution: A protected member is accessible in its own class, in all classes of the same package, and in subclasses even when they are in other packages. Non-subclasses in other packages cannot access it.

marking_points.point: Accessible in the same class and same package
Also in subclasses in other packages

questions.question: What are non-access modifiers? Give two examples.
questions.solution: Non-access modifiers give a variable or method a special property without changing its visibility. Examples: static, final.

marking_points.point: Meaning: give special properties, do not control access
